title: State Unemployment
scope: Covers BLS Local Area Unemployment Statistics: seasonally adjusted unemployment rate, employment, labor force, labor-force participation rate, and employment-population ratio for every state and D.C. Also reports QCEW average weekly wages and average monthly employment for 2025 Q4 and ETA 539 weekly UI initial and continued claims.
exclusions: Does not cover occupational wages, CPS age-sex-race detail, or advice about a job search.
heritage: Formerly Labor Market, Monthly Employment, Employment and Wages, Total Labor Force, Weekly Wages, Labor Demographics, and Unemployment Insurance
vintage_note: Rebuilt Aug 15, 2026 from BLS LAUS statewide seasonally adjusted file la.data.3.AllStatesS. Measure 03 is the unemployment rate. The U.S. civilian rate is not in this file and is not invented here. Later views compiled Aug 15, 2026 are stored under derived.secondary. Tableau companions compiled Aug 16, 2026 are stored under derived.secondary.

q: The unemployment rate by state, from BLS LAUS.
lead: Massachusetts seasonally adjusted unemployment was 4.4 percent in Jun 2026, rank 18 of 51 when states are ordered from highest rate to lowest (derived, SRC-614-01). District of Columbia was highest at 6.0 percent; South Dakota was lowest at 2.0 percent (SRC-614-01). Average weekly wages were $1,569 in the United States in 2025 Q4 (derived, SRC-614-02). Massachusetts was $1,980, rank 2 of 51 (derived, SRC-614-02). UI initial claims were 187,408 in the United States in the week ending 2026-08-08 (derived, SRC-614-03). Massachusetts filed 4,617 initial claims and 75,706 continued weeks (SRC-614-03). The Massachusetts labor-force participation rate was 65.3% in 2026-06, rank 11 of 51 (derived, SRC-614-04). The employment-population ratio was 62.4% (SRC-614-04). Employment was 3,702,521 (SRC-614-04). A CPS age-sex-race extract is not in this ledger.
